items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Willy Bryant was missing. He had taken a train back to New York when he learned that we would be flown to the Phillipines...

ctx.x: From the day we arrived in San Francisco, we were on alert which meant that we should be ready to leave at any hour, but we stayed in Frisco for one week. Spider Courance and I had a connecting room and during the week, we each drank at least a quart of whisky every day. I became quite friendly with Curby Alexander whom I had not known before he was engaged to replace Ben Smith. Curby was a billiard drinker also and could take it better than Spider, and we often drank from each other's bottle. I was so busy…

Eventually, we were notified that we would be leaving for Hamilton Field the next morning at a certain hour. Hamilton Field was a military air force base near Frisco, and the morning that the air force came to get us, Willy Bryant was missing. He had taken a train back to New York when he learned that we would be flown to the Phillipines... We stayed on the base that night and the next day we were briefed on how to use a Mae West (safety belt) if something went wrong and the plane would have to ditch (come down)…

That afternoon, we boarded a C-54 and this was a flight for our unit only. We were 12 people with a crew of 4 in a plane that could carry 60.
